Internal Network Pivot Methodology.description: Internal network penetration testing methodology — from initial foothold to full internal compromise via pivoting, infrastructure attacks, and VLAN abuse.

steps.task: Confirm shell stability and upgrade if needed (pty, socat)
Identify network interfaces and routing table — ip a && ip route
Identify reachable subnets from current host
Set up SOCKS5 proxy — ssh -D 1080 or Chisel reverse SOCKS
Configure proxychains to route tools through pivot
Test tunnel connectivity — proxychains curl http://{internal_target}
Live host discovery — arp-scan --localnet or nmap -sn via proxychains
Service fingerprinting on discovered hosts
Identify network infrastructure — routers, switches, firewalls (SNMP, CDP)
Identify VLAN boundaries via routing table and switch configs
Scan for SNMP-enabled devices — onesixtyone -c communities.txt {subnet}/24
Identify printers, VoIP phones, IoT devices (often unpatched)
DNS zone transfer attempt against internal DNS server
Identify switch port configuration — check for DTP trunk negotiation
Attempt DTP trunk mode negotiation — yersinia dtp -attack 1
If trunk established — add 802.1Q sub-interfaces for target VLANs
Double-tagging attack if native VLAN matches access VLAN
Scan VLANs reached via hopping — verify segmentation failures
ARP poisoning — MITM between critical hosts (gateway + target)
DHCP starvation + rogue DHCP — DNS redirect to attacker for phishing
LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning with Responder — capture NetNTLMv2 hashes
SMB relay if SMB signing disabled — relay captured hashes for auth
SNMP write community exploitation — modify device configs
IPv6 attacks — mitm6 for DHCPv6 DNS takeover
Default credentials on routers/switches/printers — admin:admin, cisco:cisco
SNMP enumeration — full device config extraction
Check for Cisco Smart Install enabled — ciscosmartinstall scan
VoIP exploitation — SIP enumeration, credential theft, eavesdropping
Network printer exploitation — data exfil, credential harvest, LAN access
Establish second pivot hop from newly compromised internal host
Reach isolated network segments (OT/ICS, PCI scope, management VLAN)
Identify and attack jump boxes / bastion hosts
Target internal web applications not accessible from internet
Document all network paths discovered — draw network map
